src/concordance/stigmergy.py:165: 'File writes inside a read are named' is false. In a child a shelf read calls c.search, which calls deposit, which flushes to the shared trail store every 25th deposit. The child inherits the front's pending deltas and writes them, the front later flushes the same deltas, so trails double, and a kill mid-flush leaves the store's lock for 15 s. It runs only where .env turns it on (docs/RUNBOOK.md:208), so no fresh worktree sees it. No verdict moves; ranking does. Turn deposit off in a child and pin it: a test with CONCORDANCE_STIGMERGY on and an audit hook in the child, where any open for write fails.

CELLS: src/concordance/cells.py is V3's module at 5cc7058, changed only as this plan says. A read in a cell is pure, so running it twice costs time and nothing else. No list of checks is kept: any check that touches the keeping reroutes itself. THE WALL: with cells on the front loads no sympy. _ensure_sympy is the one way it loads, and in a process with cells on it raises PowerFloorRefused. A test runs one claim per mathematics mode, one golden per domain and a rerouted shelf read through a front with cells on and finds no sympy in sys.modules. text: CORRECTION to the linux-proof note, from checker-92's review and the lead's own count of raw bytes. The note said the checkout holds the step's paths with CRLF and that the runner went over with its line ends changed. Both are wrong as written. Seven of the 13 paths hold CRLF: the seven that were already tracked. The six new files hold none, tools/cells_proof.sh among them, so the runner's blob is that path's exact bytes and the runner is the file the hash covers. The lead's check read 119 carriage returns because grep on this laptop took the pattern as empty and counted every line. The packed tree equals the checkout byte for byte on all 13 paths. The proof's result, hash and numbers stand. Also read by the lead before commit, as checker-92 asked: the corrected docstring of _root_past_the_floor states what the check bounds and gives no route.

findings: tests/test_outside_watch.py:45: the stub curl ignores every flag and fails at once, which is a closed port, not the frozen process the watch exists for, so nothing pins the watch's one bound. On a scratch copy, deploy/nh-engine-watch:12 cut from 'curl -fsS -m 10' to 'curl -sS', with the timer lines of the next finding also gone, leaves all 57 tests passing. Run here under dash with real curl against a local socket that accepts and never answers: with -m 10 both reads failed and counted in 22 s; without it the run was still hanging when killed at 30 s and counted nothing. The service is Type=oneshot, whose start has no time limit by default, so on the box that run never ends, the timer cannot fire again, and neither engine is read again. Without -f a /health answering 5xx reads as good. Fix: the stub records its arguments, or hangs unless given -m, and a test pins -f and -m 10.

tests/test_outside_watch.py:363: the timer test pins only OnUnitActiveSec=30s and WantedBy=timers.target, so deploy/nh-engine-watch.timer:4 OnBootSec=3min and :6 AccuracySec=5s can both go with all 57 passing (run, in the pack above). Read from systemd.timer(5), not run, since this laptop has no systemd: with OnUnitActiveSec alone the timer has no base after a reboot until its service has run once, so it never fires while is-active still reads active, which is all install_watch.sh's read-back asks; without AccuracySec each 30 s read may slip by up to a minute. The plan brings the stopgap in as it stands, so pin each of the timer's lines.

deploy/install_watch.sh:174: the restore's proof that it put things back is untested: with this check and :176 and :180 made no-ops on a scratch copy, all 57 pass (run). tests/test_outside_watch.py:543 makes a restore fail only through daemon-reload. With those checks gone, a restore whose copy of the stopgap failed, whose drop-in would not go, or whose timer stayed stopped prints 'WATCH restored', exits 1, and put_back at :187 deletes the snapshot, the one copy of the stopgap, where docs/HARNESS.md promises exit 3 and a kept snapshot. The code is right today; pin it with a file the restore cannot put back, a drop-in it cannot remove and a timer that will not come back, each ending at exit 3 with the snapshot kept and --undo finishing it.
